title: Deep learning for real-time detection of nasopharyngeal carcinoma during nasopharyngeal endoscopy.
summary: A YOLO-based detector identified suspected nasopharyngeal carcinoma in endoscopy frames across three centers, including a held-out external center. The evaluation is retrospective and establishes frame-level diagnostic performance, not improved patient outcomes.
ai_technology: A YOLO-based object detector identifies suspected nasopharyngeal carcinoma regions in nasopharyngeal endoscopy frames.
organization: Department of Otolaryngology, First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University, China; Guangxi Hospital Division of the First Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University, China; School of Intelligent Systems Engineering, Shenzhen Campus of Sun Yat-sen University, China; Kiang Wu Hospital, Macau; Guangzhou First People’s Hospital, China

evidence.tested: The multicenter study reports frame-level detection performance, including external-center testing, for NPC lesions during endoscopy.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective evaluation of 2,429 frames from 690 patients across three centers, with internal and external testing; no outcome-impact evidence is established.
evidence.ai_role: The detector identified suspected NPC regions in endoscopy frames and was evaluated on data from an external center.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text Methods and Results in Europe PMC and publication record.
